With the grand final set for May 16 in Vienna, jury votes and televote splits remain pivotal swing factors in this tight race.

title: Elon Musk # tweets May 8 - May 15, 2026?

eventMetadata.context_description: Gavin Newsom leads trader consensus at 24% implied probability for the 2028 Democratic presidential nomination, buoyed by his executive experience as California governor, national media profile from past Trump-era clashes, and recent fundraising at a high-profile Los Angeles event with fellow Democratic governors on April 24. Recent polls reflect a volatile, wide-open field post-2024 defeat: Kamala Harris dominated April surveys like HarrisX (50%) but fell to 13% in the May 4–7 AtlasIntel poll, where Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez surged to 26% via youth and progressive appeal. Newsom differentiates via centrist viability and West Coast base, Harris through Black voter loyalty despite loss baggage, and AOC with media savvy but House tenure limits. Consolidation hinges on 2026 midterms, early Iowa caucus polling, Biden-Clinton endorsements, and California’s June gubernatorial primary dynamics.

title: Brazil Presidential Election
description:
A presidential election is scheduled to take place in Brazil on October 4, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the listed candidate that wins this election.

This market includes any potential second round. If the result of this election isn't known by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, the market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the result of the election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the Brazilian government, specifically the Superior Electoral Court (Tribunal Superior Eleitoral, TSE) (e.g., https://dadosabertos.tse.jus.br/).

eventMetadata.context_description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva leads trader consensus at 42.5% implied probability to win Brazil's October 4, 2026, presidential election first round, with Senator Flávio Bolsonaro at 30.4%, amid polls showing a tightening race. Recent Quaest (May 8–11) and Futura (May 4–8) surveys indicate Lula ahead 38–39% to Flávio's 33–37% in first-round voting intentions, with runoffs statistically tied or narrowly favoring either candidate due to high rejection rates for both frontrunners. Lula's May 12 launch of the "Brazil Against Organized Crime" program addresses surging public security concerns, a key swing factor. Right-wing fragmentation—evident in higher market odds for Romeu Zema (7.1%) and Renan Santos (7.8%) despite lower polling—bolsters Lula's path, though volatility persists ahead of the likely October 25 runoff.
